title: fix(plugin-list,plugin-kanban,plugin-dashboard,plugin-calendar): four page blocks re-read on the data-invalidation bus (objectui#10572)
body:
Fixes #10572
Clause-②: no

## What this does

All five page-embeddable data blocks on objectui#10572 now re-read when the data-invalidation bus (`notifyDataChanged` from `@object-ui/react`) reports a change to the object they query. Each renderer uses the shape from PR objectui#10494: its fetch effect names the `useDataInvalidation` nonce for its own object, and a `'*'` change matches too. There is no host counter prop, no relay and no `key=` remount. There is one commit per package; the form commit came in a second round, after the seat ruled on the fork below. A third change, in the app-shell object page, makes one console write reach the list as one read (see below).

| package | renderer | subscribed when |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `@object-ui/plugin-list` | `ListView` (`list-view`, `view:list`) | the list fetches for itself (no inline `data`, no gantt that owns its endpoint) |
| `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` | `ObjectKanban` | no external, bound or inline cards |
| `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` | `ObjectMetricWidget` (`object-metric`) | a data source and an `objectName` |
| `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` | `ObjectCalendar` | the `object` provider and no external events |
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | the object page `ObjectView` (host, not a reader) | n/a: it hands the console's refresh counter to its readers in the same commit |
| `@object-ui/plugin-form` | `ObjectForm` (`object-form`, edit and view) | a `recordId`, not create mode, no inline fields; keyed on the record, so another record's change reads nothing |

## Census: real `SchemaRenderer`, real registrations, counting fake data source

These are reads on mount, then reads after `notifyDataChanged({ objectName: '*' })`. It is a one-off probe (not committed), run before and after the change.

| block | before (at base `f169a030a`) | after (at `1e6aad5a8`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `object-grid` (control) | 1 → 2 | 1 → 2 |
| `object-chart` (control) | 1 → 2 | 1 → 2 |
| `detail-view` (control) | 1 → 2 | 1 → 2 |
| `list-view` | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** |
| `view:list` | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** |
| `object-kanban` | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** |
| `object-metric` | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** |
| `object-calendar` | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** |
| `object-form`, edit mode | 1 → 1 | **1 → 2** when pristine (round 2, pinned below) |

For list, kanban, metric and calendar, the committed pins are per package, beside each renderer (`*.invalidationRefetch-10572.test.tsx`); the form's pins are in their own section below. Each renders through `SchemaRenderer` and that package's own registration, and asserts four things. A `'*'` change costs exactly one re-read. A change to the block's own object (record-scoped) costs one. A change to another object costs none. For list and kanban, inline rows query nothing. The cross-package census stays a probe because a committed version would import `plugin-grid`, `plugin-charts` and `plugin-detail` from a package that doesn't declare them (`check:phantom-deps`).

**Ablation for those four** (fix committed first; the trap restores from `HEAD`). I removed `invalidationNonce` from the four dependency lists and checked on disk that each anchor went from 1 to 0. The four pin files then gave `Tests 8 failed | 2 passed (10)`; the 2 passes are the inline-rows cases, which assert no query either way. After the restore, `git diff HEAD` is empty and all four blob hashes match `HEAD`.

## `object-form`: re-read gated on pristine

A bare re-read overwrote a dirty field. I measured this with a probe: I typed `User typed` into `name`, the server's value moved to `Server v2`, and I fired the bus. Both refetch variants broke the edit:

- **Naive re-read:** it takes the `Loading form...` branch, which unmounts the form.
- **Silent re-read (no loading flip):** the form renderer resets by value to the new `defaultValues`.

Either way the input read `Server v2`, and the re-read would also have advanced the OCC token the save sends. The seat ruled option A, gate on pristine (comment 5832287152 on the card):

- **Pristine:** the form re-reads in place. The loading branch is skipped for a bus re-read, so nothing is remounted.
- **Dirty:** the change is held. The typed values and the `ifMatch` token the edit started from both stay, so a real conflict still surfaces through the existing conflict dialog at save. One re-read is replayed once the form is pristine again, which happens either through the form renderer's existing `onDirtyChange(false)` (a reset or a revert) or when this form's save lands.

Dirtiness is read from that existing channel into a private ref, and `ObjectForm` passes `onDirtyChange` on both the flat and the sectioned form schemas. It is an existing `FormSchema` member, so nothing new is declared. The components form renderer is untouched.

Pins are in `ObjectForm.invalidationRefetch-10572.test.tsx`, through `SchemaRenderer` and the real registration:

- (a) A pristine form re-reads 1 → 2, and the same input node shows `Server v2`.
- (b) On both the flat and the sectioned paths, a dirty `User typed` survives the bus event with no read, and the save sends `ifMatch` equal to the original `updated_at`.
- (c) After the dirty edit is saved, two held changes replay as exactly one read. After it is reverted to pristine, one read is replayed.
- (d) A change scoped to another record, or to another object, reads nothing.

Ablation (the fix was committed first, and a trap restores from `HEAD`):

- Removing the dirty gate gives `Tests 4 failed | 2 passed (6)`: both (b) cases and both (c) cases fail.
- Making every bus re-read take the loading branch gives `Tests 1 failed | 5 passed (6)`: case (a) fails.

Each leg's anchor count went from 1 to 0 on disk, and after each restore `git diff HEAD` was empty. My first ablation attempt counted a multi-line anchor with `grep -c`, which cannot match across lines. It aborted before changing anything, and I reran it with exact-string counts.

## One console write, one list read: the app-shell object page

CI went red on `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx`: the grid, kanban and gantt/chart-whitelist cases each read 2 where the pin expects 1. The cause was the host, not `ListView`.

- **Both signals, same tick:** the console's undo and redo bump `externalRefreshKey` and call `notifyDataChanged` in the same tick.
- **The mirror:** the object page used to copy `externalRefreshKey` into its own `refreshKey` through a passive effect, one commit later.
- **Two reads:** now that `ListView` reads the bus, it saw the bus nonce in one commit and `refreshTrigger` in the next, and read twice.

PR objectui#10494's contract is that a writer's two notices land in one render. Every other writer already does that: `refreshData`, plugin-view's `announceOwnWrite` and `onMutation`, and the console bridge.

The fix is the seat's option H, and there is no mirror left. The page's own counter becomes `ownRefreshKey`. `refreshKey` is now `ownRefreshKey + externalRefreshKey`, summed in the render that receives the prop. Every existing reader keeps its name and sees an external bump in that same commit: the list's `refreshTrigger`, the saved-view and draft read, the list-view metadata read, the record-count probe, and the environment entitlements. `ListView` keeps its bus read, with no gate and no debounce.

Pins:

- `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx` is unchanged and 5/5 green, including the realtime case.
- `ObjectView.externalRefreshSum-10572.test.tsx` adds three cases on the same harness. An undo-shaped write (bump plus bus notice) costs one list read and one record-count read. A counter-only bump with nothing on the bus still re-reads the list once and the count once. A realtime change costs one list read.

**Reverse-verify:** I restored the mirror-only `ObjectView.tsx` from before this change. The pins gave `Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8)`: the three #10035 list cases and the undo-shaped case went red. After the restore, `git diff HEAD` was empty and the blob hash matched.

## Acceptance notes

- `ObjectCalendar` shows its `Loading calendar…` placeholder during a re-read, as its existing `onMutation` refresh already does. `currentDate` and the view mode live in `ObjectCalendar` state and survive. `ListView` uses `RefreshIndicator` over the current rows. The board and the metric keep their surfaces mounted.
- `ListView`, `ObjectKanban` and `ObjectCalendar` also keep their `dataSource.onMutation` subscriptions. A data-source write reaches both that subscription and the bus bridge in the same synchronous dispatch, so React batches the two state bumps into one effect run.
- Probed with the same census and left stale (not changed here; reported on the card): `object-timeline` 1 → 1, `object-gallery` 1 → 1, `object-map` 2 → 2, `element:number` 1 → 1, `element:repeater` 1 → 1.
- `origin/main` was merged once before opening, as the claim asked, so the diff can merge with draft PR objectui#10597. The `ListView` change is one declaration above the fetch effect plus one dependency-list name.

## Gates

Round 4 is at `190d86bfc`, after one more `origin/main` merge (`d9bef0395`, no conflicts). The five package suites ran at `d9bef0395`; the only later commit removes two unused imports from the new app-shell pin, and those pins were re-run at `190d86bfc`.

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| app-shell test files naming `ObjectView`, `refreshKey` or `externalRefreshKey` | 75 files, 869 tests passed |
| `plugin-list` | 95 files, 1134 tests passed |
| `plugin-kanban` | 63 files, 416 tests passed |
| `plugin-dashboard` | 130 files, 1246 tests passed |
| `plugin-calendar` | 45 files, 323 tests passed |
| `plugin-form` | 121 files, 1274 passed and 1 skipped |
| app-shell `type-check` | exit 0 |
| app-shell `lint` | exit 0, 0 errors |

The first app-shell lint run found 2 unused imports in the new pin, which I removed in `190d86bfc`. These cheap gates all exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` (12 source files of 6 released packages, 6 changesets declared), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:test-path-roots` and `check:vi-mock-specifiers`.

Earlier rounds: `type-check` and `lint` for the five plugin packages are green (round 1 at `6e70f10a2`; plugin-form and plugin-list in round 2 at `6caed987d`).

I didn't run the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` locally; CI runs them.
